newsitem.title: UK: IRA ceasefire hopes unfounded - British minister.
newsitem.headline: IRA ceasefire hopes unfounded - British minister.

text.p: Speculation that the Irish Republican Army may be about to call a fresh truce in its guerrilla war to end British rule in Northern Ireland appears unjustified, a British minister said on Thursday.

"I think we may for once be able to take Mr Adams and Mr McGuinness at their word when they assure us that talk of a renewal of the ceasefire is unfounded," Sir John Wheeler, Northern Ireland Office security minister, said in a London speech.
Gerry Adams and Martin McGuinness are respectively the leader and chief strategist of Sinn Fein, the political wing of the IRA.
They have dampened hopes of a resumption of the 19-month ceasefire which the IRA ended last February with a bomb explosion in London's Docklands area in which two people died.
Since the Docklands explosion, there has been a series of other bomb blasts in mainland Britain, the last of which wrecked the centre of the northern city of Manchester in June.

Hopes of a new ceasefire were raised by British newspaper reports last month suggesting the IRA was planning a secret conference at which it might call another ceasefire to allow Sinn Fein to take part in all-party talks on the province's future.
Britain and Ireland have insisted there can be no seat at the table for Sinn Fein until the IRA renounces the use of violence in its campaign for a united Ireland.
Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said last week that a new ceasefire was inevitable eventually, but he could not say if it would be called in the short term.
Wheeler, stressing that he had no inside knowledge on the possibility of a ceasefire, said: "Given the evidence, the signs are not hopeful."

He pointed to the seizure by police in London on September 23 of almost 10 tonnes of home-made explosive, together with significant amounts of Semtex, arms and ammunition, believed to have been stored by an IRA cell.
"This material was clearly intended for use in a terrorist "spectacular' on the lines of those at Docklands and Manchester," Wheeler said.
"How can they (Sinn Fein leaders) reconcile their rhetoric for peace with the Provisional IRA's preparations for murder?"

He said that in addition to its bomb attacks, the IRA was continuing to train its members, to develop and test improved weaponry and to mount vigilante patrols dispensing summary justice in Roman Catholic areas of Northern Ireland.
